articles.title: Physicists create Bose–Einstein condensate from ultracold polar molecules
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: Bose–Einstein condensates are states of matter that form when particles called bosons are cooled to temperatures that are only a fraction of a degree above absolute zero (i.e., 0 Kelvin [-460°F]). In these states, particles occupy the same quantum state and exhibit interesting collective behaviors, essentially behaving as if they were a single "super-particle."

articles.title: Your gut may help your brain decide what to remember
articles.summary: Signals traveling from the gut to the brain may help turn meals into lasting memories. Rats showed stronger memory activity after consuming nutritious foods, but not after drinking sweet liquids with little or no nutritional value. Blocking the vagus nerve erased this effect and made it harder for the animals to remember where food had been located. Over time, diets high in fat and sugar also weakened this memory system.

articles.title: Can’t sleep in the heat? These 8 tricks could save your night
articles.summary: Sleeping well during a heatwave starts with stopping the home from overheating. Moving to a cooler room, choosing light bedding and using fans or ice packs safely can also make hot nights more manageable.
